correctness.rationale: The exact hypergeometric second moments independently yield \(T_i^{\pm}\) and positive rates. The adjacent first-step harmonic identity and its gamma product prove the finite-N claim for every d and k. Symmetric Gamma weights and monotonic factors prove the strict finite-N group-size ordering. A fixed-d Stirling expansion, a unique strictly concave Laplace saddle and the fixed-k numerator yield the asymptotic with explicit \(C_d\) and \(O(N^{-1})\) relative error. An artanh integral proves \(I_d>J_d\) and monotonic I_d with endpoints. Running verify.py checked 440 exact rational finite-state identities and 8 supplementary large-N comparisons; the latter are not proofs of infinite behavior.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The statement is neither a mere reformulation of macroscopic drift nor covered by the published Gaussian approximation. The standard birth–death recurrence is acknowledged; the scientific claim is the explicit closed action and its strict mismatch with central diffusion extrapolation. A more general uninspected WKB result remains a possible implication risk.

originality.rationale: Material inspection of the 2026 complete-hypergraph primary source (transition Eq.24 and mean-field Eq.33), the 2025 group-driven voter primary analysis (Appendix B, supplemental S16–S20), the 2026 consensus-time follow-up, the 2009 nonlinear q-voter backward-diffusion paper, and the 2025 biased q-voter Section III.D found no stated exact finite-N hypergeometric fixation sum plus fixed-degree sharp barrier and prefactor. The central Gaussian exit approximation in the closest 2025 paper is not a global large-deviation theorem, and its rare-minority extrapolation has a rigorously different exponent. Standard birth–death products and Laplace asymptotics are preexisting methods; originality rests on this model-specific closed identification and quantified nonuniformity. Broader WKB derivations remain a named risk.
residual_risks: General birth–death chain WKB analyses or asymptotic binomial identities may imply the formula once the finite transition rates are supplied; this equivalence was not exhaustively resolved.
The evidence supports novelty relative to inspected closely matched works, not an assertion of literature-wide priority.
The comparison with the 2025 Gaussian formula is for endpoint extrapolation and does not contest central-window accuracy.

value.rationale: Rare-opinion conversion is a natural distinct question from mean consensus time and the central diffusion sigmoid. The result supplies an all-N exact probability, sharp fixed-degree rare-event action and prefactor, and a principled boundary for when a known Gaussian approximation ceases to predict exponentially small probabilities. The group-size monotonicity and sharp distinction are structural, not an arbitrary numerical special case. No downstream social prediction or paper-sized application is assumed.
